raised.claim: The planner checks scope for existing issues but does not check it for rows filed with a new issue.
raised.why_it_breaks: A zero-candidate row routed to a new issue scoped to `candidates_count > 0` passes the key check, appears in the issue's initial examples, and is recorded against that issue even though the same verdict would be rejected on the next run.

raised.claim: The saturation guard does not count rows already accepted for the same issue in the current plan.
raised.why_it_breaks: If an issue starts at 11 post-creation rows and five matching verdicts target it, all five see the same count of 11 and are accepted, bringing the issue to 16 instead of stopping at 12.

raised.claim: An enumerated cohort legalizes a whole-class predicate even though the predicate can still match rows outside that cohort.
raised.why_it_breaks: A scope with `beer_ids: [1]` and `where: [{col: 'review_class', op: '=', value: 'matcher_bug'}]` passes validation, and a later `matcher_bug` row with ID 2 passes via the `where` branch. Adding one ID therefore bypasses the whole-class guard without narrowing future attachments.

raised.claim: The legality check treats any non-class predicate as narrowing, even when it is true for every eligible row.
raised.why_it_breaks: A `matcher_bug` class filter combined with `fail_count >= 1` passes the guard but still covers the whole class: the failure upsert starts every row at 1 and increments it on repeat failures.

raised.claim: The parser trusts the first scope-looking block in the full issue body, which can come from model-authored prose rather than the structured field.
raised.why_it_breaks: The job appends the generated block after the model's Markdown. If that Markdown already contains a `triage-scope` example, the next run uses the example instead of the generated block; if the first block is malformed, the issue is treated as unscoped despite the valid block below it.

raised.quote:
const parsed = ScopeSchema.safeParse(JSON.parse(m[1]));
    return parsed.success ? parsed.data : null;
raised.claim: Existing issue scopes are checked for schema validity but not for the legality required of new proposals.
raised.why_it_breaks: If a backfilled or manually edited issue gets a block whose only predicate is `review_class = matcher_bug`, the block parses successfully and every `matcher_bug` verdict can attach while the issue is below the saturation threshold.

raised.quote:
const probe = probes.get(verdict.beer_id);
      const proved = probe?.brewery === '' || probe?.name === '';
raised.claim: An empty result from one probe is treated as absence evidence even when the other probe returns the beer.
raised.why_it_breaks: If the scraped brewery spelling returns nothing but the name-only search returns the matching beer, `proved` is still true and a mistaken `not_on_untappd` verdict survives, blocking the metered web fallback for a beer the probe found.

raised.claim: Guard counters are hidden whenever the model emits a verdict for every row, even if the planner rejects every verdict.
raised.why_it_breaks: If all 50 rows are routed to saturated issues, `covered` is still 50 because it is calculated from the model output. The run skips all 50 with no `guardHits` log, so an operator cannot see the reason for the stalled batch.

raised.claim: The new absence downgrade feeds `matcher_bug` verdicts into the quiet path that counts every non-absence verdict as `wontfix`.
raised.why_it_breaks: If 10 absence verdicts are downgraded because no probe ran, the database records 10 `matcher_bug` rows, but the daily digest reports 10 `wontfix` rows.

raised.quote:
`SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM enrich_failures
        WHERE issue_number = ? AND reviewed_at > ?`,
raised.claim: The saturation query compares timestamp strings rather than instants.
raised.why_it_breaks: GitHub can supply `2026-08-14T06:00:00Z`, while the job stores `2026-08-14T06:00:00.500Z`. The review is half a second later, but SQLite sorts `.` before `Z` and excludes it from the count.

raised.quote:
review_class       = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.review_class END,
       review_note        = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.review_note END,
       reviewed_at        = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.reviewed_at END`,
raised.claim: Reopening a failure clears its review but leaves the new authoritative issue link behind.
raised.why_it_breaks: If a row linked to #347 moves from zero candidates to three, its class, note, and review timestamp are cleared, but an issue-number lookup still reports it against #347 until the row is reviewed again.

raised.quote:
`SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM enrich_failures
        WHERE issue_number = ? AND reviewed_at > ?`,
raised.claim: The saturation signal measures surviving failure rows, so reopening or clearing a failure gives an issue capacity back without removing anything from GitHub.
raised.why_it_breaks: An issue that has received 12 post-creation attachments becomes eligible again after one of those failures matches and is deleted. It can then receive a 13th attachment even though all 12 earlier examples remain on the issue.

raised.quote:
UPDATE enrich_failures
     SET issue_number = CAST(substr(review_note, instr(review_note, '→ #') + 3) AS INTEGER)
   WHERE review_note LIKE '%→ #%'
     AND CAST(substr(review_note, instr(review_note, '→ #') + 3) AS INTEGER) > 0;
raised.claim: The backfill promotes the first arrow-number mention anywhere in a free-text note to the authoritative issue link.
raised.why_it_breaks: A note such as `compare alias → #12; actual gap → #347` backfills #12 even though #347 is the appended attachment suffix. A quiet note containing only an incidental arrow-number mention can likewise create a link where no attachment occurred.

raised.claim: The strict tool schema accepts scope terms that the runtime analysis schema rejects.
raised.why_it_breaks: A term such as `{col: 'candidates_count', op: '>', value: '0'}` is valid under the tool schema but fails `ScopeSchema`, so one tool-valid proposal can invalidate an otherwise usable analysis payload.

raised.claim: The prompt's body truncation can hide the appended scope while the planner still enforces it.
raised.why_it_breaks: For an issue with more than 2,000 characters of prose before its generated scope, the model sees the issue title and description but not its row constraints. It can repeatedly route a row based on those visible fields only to have the planner reject it.

raised.claim: The persisted issue link is not conditional on the row still matching the snapshot used by the scope guard.
raised.why_it_breaks: If enrichment updates a row from three candidates to zero during the LLM or GitHub await, a verdict for an issue scoped to `candidates_count > 0` can still be planned from the old row and then written onto the current row because the update only checks `beer_id`.
